differential_evidence.description: Event precipitant and semiology (best obtained by a detailed witness account or home video): spells triggered by crying/frustration with expiratory apnea and rapid recovery → supports breath‑holding; unprovoked tonic activity or stereotyped automatisms → supports seizure.
Post‑event features: prolonged confusion, postictal lethargy, tongue biting or incontinence → favors seizure; rapid normalization without a postictal period → favors breath‑holding.

Cardiac examination / baseline oxygenation: resting central cyanosis, murmurs, poor growth, clubbing, or abnormal baseline pulse oximetry → favors structural cardiac disease; normal cardiac exam and normal resting SpO2 → argues against structural cyanosis.

Targeted investigations: abnormal EEG/video‑EEG → supports seizure; abnormal ECG/Holter or echocardiogram → supports cardiac cause; iron deficiency / low hemoglobin (and improvement of spells with iron therapy) → supports breath‑holding spells (association with iron deficiency anemia).
